evidence: repro_D/d01_reactivating.py: one cell carrying only its IE productive marker via run_one() with the packaged catalogue -> EBV reactivating (intended); HHV-6A (U90 HUM_HERP6_HHV6_p24) reactivating; HHV-6B (U95) reactivating; HHV-7 (U90 gp81) reactivating; VZV (ORF62 gp63) reactivating; all with latency_not_observable=True; only HCMV -> indeterminate. The HCMV exclusion is a one-name allow-list; the same 'latency mimics IE expression' argument applies to VZV (ORF62/ORF63/ORF4 transcripts detected in latent ganglia: Cohrs 1996 J Virol 70:2789; Nagel 2011; contested by Depledge 2018 post-mortem RNA-seq finding only VLT) and HHV-6 (ciHHV-6 individuals express U90/IE1A most highly in GTEx; secondary source hhv-6foundation.org summary, primary paper unverified). For latency_observable=false viruses 'reactivating' is a presence-only call with no latency anchor, i.e. the non-specific call PROG-12 rejected for HCMV. docs/output_reference.md:463 says 'Never emitted for HCMV' only.
proposed_fix: Gate reactivating on latency_observable_in_rna (or add a per-virus reactivation_applicable catalogue column); at minimum add VZV/HHV-6A/6B/HHV-7 to REACTIVATION_NOT_APPLICABLE, report n_cells_reactivating=not_applicable, and document in the States table.

evidence: repro_D/d01_reactivating.py part 2: VZV index containing only ORF62 (4 of 5 catalogue markers unresolved): run_one logs WARNING 'calls use the reduced marker set' and still emits state=reactivating; summary n_cells_reactivating=1, caveat only '4 of 5 catalogue markers did not resolve'. reactivating = IE evidence AND absence of any later productive group; when the later markers are the unresolved ones, later_cols is empty and every IE-positive cell is reactivating (absence unobservable). Likewise productive>=min_breadth may be unreachable and latency_observable is a catalogue property, not an index property. PROG-14 'fail loudly' only warns; states are emitted as normal.
proposed_fix: In run_one, if no resolved non-IE productive marker exists force reactivating_applicable=False; if fewer than min_breadth productive groups resolved flag productive unreachable; add a summary column naming which classes were assessable on this index.

evidence: Comment states 'HHV-6A/6B share ~95% identity; HSV-1/2 share ~80%'. Lookup: HHV-6A vs HHV-6B overall nucleotide identity is ~90% (Dominguez et al. 1999 J Virol, PMC112820; most divergent regions: direct repeats 85%, U86-U100 region 72%; immediate-early genes ~70%). The ~95% figure is not supported (strain-pair figures: 98% U1102 vs HHV-6A, 89% Z29 vs HHV-6B). HSV-1/2 '~80%': unverified. The ratio-50 threshold rationale rests on these numbers; the HHV-6 IE divergence (~70%) also means IE-marker cross-mapping between 6A/6B is lower than the comment implies.
proposed_fix: Cite the source and use ~90% (with the divergent-region caveat); mark HSV-1/2 figure with its citation or 'unverified'.

evidence: repro_D/d10_anello_wrap_gene_cdna.py: for the panel's one origin-spanning gene (KU243129.1, join(2677..2824,1..80)) the anellovirus GTF keeps the exons in transcript order (the test asserts this), but running the same GTF through the splitter kb ref uses (ngs_tools.gtf.genes_and_transcripts_from_gtf + fasta.split_genomic_fasta_to_cdna) gives 'indexed cDNA == transcript-order CDS: False' and '== genomic-order [1:80]+[2677:2824]: True'. The PLAN ANELLO-05 note ('parser never re-sorts') protects the GTF only; the indexed transcript is transposed. The anellovirus GTF is also not passed through gtf_normalise, so the 'wrap_native' tag that records exactly this for EBV LMP-2A/2B is absent. Impact: one gene, junction-spanning reads only; the test (tests/test_anellovirus_reference.py:309) asserts the GTF, not the cDNA.
proposed_fix: Tag the row (viralscan_norm "wrap_native") or run normalise_gtf_file on the anellovirus GTF; add a test through ngs_tools, or document as the same known limitation as HBV P/S.

evidence: repro_D/d09_anello_virus_summary.py: accessions A (3000 reads, identity 0.99, query coverage 0.98) + B, C (3 reads each, 0.80 / 0.40) -> alignment_median_identity=0.8, alignment_median_query_coverage=0.4 (read-weighted ~0.99 / ~0.98). The docstring says fractions are read-weighted so 'one accession with three reads cannot outvote one with three thousand', yet identity and query coverage are unweighted medians of per-accession medians (documented as such at docs/output_reference.md:212, so this is a design weakness, not a doc error): a few reads on off-target accessions of a related genus can dominate the 'alignment evidence quality' columns that label calls.
proposed_fix: Use a read-weighted median (pool per-read values or weight by reads) for identity/query_coverage, or report both.

evidence: Comment says both multimap caps are 100 'so every secondary record reaches the BAM and NH is the true count'. STAR's --outFilterMultimapNmax semantics (STAR manual): reads mapping to MORE than 100 loci get no alignments at all and are counted as 'mapped to too many loci'. In a ~2,000-contig panel clustered only at 95% ANI, a read from a conserved element (e.g. a GC-rich UTR shared across genera) can exceed 100 placements and silently disappears from BAM, accession_metrics and virus_molecules (undercount precisely for the most conserved evidence; no 'too many loci' count is surfaced). Not reproduced here (needs a STAR run; no STAR/index offline) - unverified magnitude.
proposed_fix: Surface Log.final.out 'too many loci' reads in the anello_alignment tables, or raise the caps / document the limitation; measure on the covid census run.

evidence: HHV-7 U42 is labelled kinetic_class=immediate_early (kinetic_pmid 10573164) while its note says 'multifunctional expression regulator; lytic'. PMID 10573164 is 'Temporal mapping of transcripts in human herpesvirus-7' (J Gen Virol 1999;80:2705; abstract retrieved via eutils: alpha/beta/gamma cascade in productively infected T cells, no transcripts in PBMC of healthy adults); the abstract does not say which ORFs are alpha, so U42=IE is unverified. Because call_cell_programme treats IE-class productive markers as 'reactivating'-eligible (D-01), a single U42 molecule in an HHV-7 cell yields 'reactivating'. proposed_fix: Verify against the full text or mark the class 'unclassified' until a primary source is read; add a catalogue test that IE-class rows cite a retrieved source.
